analysis_steps.goal: Build the parametric lens model and measure magnifications

method.value: LENSTOOL parametric model with PIEMD halos and 165 cluster members; ALMA and VLA magnifications from the ratio of image-plane to source-plane area, with 300 resamplings of the MCMC posterior

evidence.quote: we measured magnifications simply by taking the ratio of image-plane to source-plane area.
we resampled 300 iterations uniformly from the MCMC-derived posterior distribution, resulting in an approximately Gaussian distribution of magnifications.

key_parameters.value: Two cluster-scale PIEMD halos plus 165 cluster members; uniform priors with +/-5'' position range, ellipticity 0 to 0.85, maximum velocity dispersion 800 km/s, maximum core radius 20'' (~100 kpc); halo cut radii fixed to 1000 kpc

evidence.quote: Uniform priors were used for these parameters, including a wide range of $\pm 5\ensuremath{''}$ in $x$ and $y$ position from the approximate center of both cluster cores,
As their cut/truncation radii are poorly constrained, these were fixed to values of 1000 kpc.

key_parameters.value: DSFG-3 redshift left free (prior z = 2.0 - 2.2), giving z_geom = 2.11 +/- 0.01

evidence.quote: allowed the redshift to vary from $z=2.0 - 2.2$ in the final model.

assumptions.value: Cluster-member scaling relation normalized to L* galaxy (m_F200W = 17.0 AB) with sigma_0* = 120 km/s, r_core* = 0.15 kpc, r_cut* = 30 kpc

evidence.quote: The power law was normalized such that a characteristic $L_\star$ galaxy at the redshift of the cluster ($m_{\rm F200W} = 17.0$ AB mag) has a velocity dispersion of $\sigma_0^\star = 120~{\rm km~s}^{-1}$,

evidence.quote: In this work, we adopt the median of each parameter’s posterior distribution
